newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN AND DORTMUND EAGER FOR SHOWDOWN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BAYERN AND DORTMUND EAGER FOR SHOWDOWN.

text.p: Bayern Munich and reigning champions Borussia Dortmund have both overcome their early-season problems just in time for their top-of-the-table German first division clash on Sunday.

After a disappointing early exit from the UEFA Cup which they won last season, Bayern, who have won the German title a record 13 times, have stopped their internal squabbling and lifted their form before Sunday evening's game.

Dortmund travel to Munich with an extra spring in their step after upsetting Atletico Madrid 1-0 in Spain in the Champions' League in midweek. The victory effectively guaranteed Borussia a place in the European Cup quarter-finals.
Bayern chairman Franz Beckenbauer, however, has warned his players that they cannot count on injury-hit Dortmund being tired after their European success.
"They will be fresher than they were before the game in Madrid," the former World Cup-winning captain and coach said.
Dortmund trainer Ottmar Hitzfeld, whose team have been struggling with injuries all season, added: "My team has won back the belief that they can also beat big teams."
After 10 games, Dortmund are fourth in the table, four points behind Bayern who moved level on points with leaders VfB Stuttgart last weekend with a 4-2 victory at Cologne.

That game included two goals from Germany captain Juergen Klinsmann who had been under fire for failing to score in previous weeks. With a confident Klinsmann in their ranks and better team spirit, Bayern have an extra edge to their play.
"Everything is right with us now," midfielder Mario Basler said. "Everyone is waiting to see more trouble here. For that reason we are even closer together."
The cream of German soccer will be on display in Munich's Olympic stadium which is expecting a capacity 63,000 crowd.

Some 14 of Germany's Euro 96-winning squad earn their living at the two clubs although not all of them are fit for the match, most notably Dortmund's injured libero Matthias Sammer -- the inspiration behind Germany's triumph in England.
Many of the players know each other well from national team duty. But there is fierce rivalry between the two teams and particular individuals.
Dortmund were defeated 1-0 in the corresponding match last season which ended with Bayern midfielder Mehmet Scholl taking a swipe at Dortmund striker Stephane Chapuisat.

"Last year we lost 1-0 and did not put up much of a show, " said Dortmund wing-back Stefan Reuter, a former Bayern player. "But if we play with the same confidence that we did in Madrid nothing will happen to us."
Dortmund are hoping that midfielder playmaker Andy Moeller will be fit enough to return after a leg muscle injury.
The Bavarians will be without international wing-back Christian Ziege and defender Thomas Helmer who both have long-term injuries. Basler is also doubtful because of a calf muscle injury.
